description:
Headland is tackling Field Shift—building a farmer-centric decision-support tool that fuses NASA Earth observations (SMAP, ECOSTRESS, GPM, Landsat) with local soil and crop constraints to compare resilient rotation strategies.

Driven by a background in AI, data science, geospatial pipelines, and full-stack development, this project bridges orbital foresight with ground-level field logic to make climate adaptation practical, visual, and explainable.
summary: Headland is a global, physics-based agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers evaluate and adapt multi-season crop rotations under shifting climate anomalies.   Operating at any latitude and longitude on Earth, Headland fuses multi-scale Earth observations—30 years of daily climate and root-zone wetness from NASA POWER, 30-meter vegetation greenness from NASA Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) via Microsoft Planetary Computer to detect bare-field vulnerability windows, 30-meter terrain slope from NASADEM for RUSLE erosion modeling, and NASA GIBS satellite imagery. Using vectorized FAO-56 daily water-balance physics and a CVaR linear programming optimizer, the engine simulates 512 candidate rotation sequences across 30 historical analog years in under 0.2 seconds.   Farmers can interactively stress-test their current rotation against drought and heat shocks while comparing water-conserving and soil-regenerating alternatives. By translating orbital telemetry into plain-language decision cards and local verification checklists, Headland strengthens soil health and water resilience without replacing generational farmer judgment.
details:
Overview & Problem Context

Generational farmers hold deep intuition about their land, but shifting temperatures, erratic rainfall, depleting groundwater, and soil degradation are breaking historical planting calendars. Headland ("Where orbital foresight meets the field edge") is a global, coordinate-agnostic agricultural decision-support platform built for the Field Shift challenge. Rather than replacing farmer judgment with opaque predictions, Headland acts as an interactive co-pilot—allowing anyone at any latitude and longitude on Earth to compare multi-season crop rotation strategies under real climate anomalies.

How It Works: Multi-Scale Data Fusion & Physics Engine

To operate globally without requiring pre-trained regional neural networks, Headland harmonizes satellite Earth observations across multiple spatial resolutions (from 30 meters to 50 km) with published agricultural physics:

  1. Multi-Scale Earth Observation Ingestion:
    • NASA POWER API (Daily AG Community): Pulls 30 years of daily climate history (1996–2025), Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration ($ET_0$), and root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT) to establish local climatological baselines.
    • NASA Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS v2) via Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC: Analyzes 30-meter monthly NDVI greenness trajectories to detect Bare-Field Vulnerability Windows (NDVI < 0.25) where soil is exposed to wind and rain erosion.
    • NASADEM (30 m): Extracts local elevation and terrain slope gradients to compute RUSLE relative soil erosion risk.
    • Meteomatics & Open-Meteo APIs: Provide high-resolution (down to 1 km) 14-day forecasts for mid-season tactical advisories.
    • ISRIC SoilGrids 2.0 & NASA GIBS: Supply global soil texture fractions and true-color orbital basemap imagery.
    • Using NumPy-vectorized FAO-56 daily root-zone water-balance physics, Saxton & Rawls soil hydraulics, and SCS Curve Number runoff, Headland simulates 512 candidate 3-season rotation sequences across 30 historical analog years in under 0.2 seconds.
    • Unlike single-season tools, Headland tracks inter-season soil memory: residual nitrogen (kg/ha) from legumes and cover crops carries forward into subsequent seasons, botanical families are rotated to disrupt pest cycles, and bare-field windows are closed with cover crops.
    • A Rockafellar & Uryasev Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) linear programming solver evaluates trade-offs across farmer priorities and generates three side-by-side strategies: Current Rotation (Baseline), Climate-Smart Water Shield, and Soil-Regenerating & Pest-Break Cycle.
    • Interactive What-If Climate Shock Sliders (Δ Rainfall % and Δ Temperature °C) let users stress-test rotations live against drought and heat anomalies.

Creativity, Impact & Human-Centered Factors Considered

  • Universal by Construction: By anchoring anomalies to each coordinate's own 30-year baseline and physical water balance, Headland adapts seamlessly from semi-arid Indian Vertisols to North American prairie soils or Mediterranean valleys without regional bias.
  • Explainability & Scientific Guardrails: Every recommendation generates a plain-English Farmer Decision Card (Weather Fit, Soil Impact, and Local Extension Checklist) backed by traceable rule IDs (R-WATER-01, R-SOIL-02), a scientific glossary (ET₀, NDVI, RUSLE), and explicit reminders of satellite-to-ground resolution limits.
  • Offline & Low-Bandwidth Resilience: Built-in disk caching and snapshot bundles allow complete offline execution in under 2.5 seconds for field extension officers working in low-connectivity areas.

Tools, Languages & Software Stack

  • Backend & Physics Engine: Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, NumPy, SciPy (linprog), Pandas, Uvicorn
  • Geospatial & Data Clients: pystac-client, planetary-computer, meteomatics, httpx, Leaflet.js (with NASA GIBS tiles), Chart.js
  • Frontend & Deployment: Responsive HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript single-page dashboard, Docker & Docker Compose, pytest (24/24 automated acceptance tests, 94% engine coverage)

Acknowledgments & Tool Disclosure

AI coding and ideation assistants were used during development to accelerate FastAPI scaffolding, frontend layout styling, and technical documentation; all agronomic equations, physical simulations, NASA data integrations, and automated verification tests were independently validated.

  • Full source code: https://github.com/prathamnagar96/HeadLand.git
